name: Machine Learning & Deep Learning Foundations
summary: The mathematics and training mechanics underneath everything else: optimisation, backpropagation, regularisation, and the failure modes that look like bugs but are statistics.
competencies: Classical baselines as a check on learned models

name: Transformers & Language Models
summary: How attention actually computes, what pretraining and fine-tuning change, and where context length, tokenisation, and decoding strategy decide behaviour.
competencies: Attention and positional encoding from first principles
Decoding strategies and their effect on reliability

name: AI Application Engineering
summary: Turning a model call into a system: prompt and context design, retrieval, structured output, caching, cost control, and the boring parts that decide whether it survives contact with users.
competencies: Prompt and context engineering under token budgets

name: Agents, Tools & MCP
summary: Multi-step systems that call tools and act. Where I already have professional work: governed data access through Model Context Protocol servers with validation and enforced limits.
competencies: Query validation, injection prevention, row limits
Human approval gates in agentic workflows

name: MLOps, Serving & Infrastructure
summary: Getting a model into a place where other people can depend on it, and keeping it there: packaging, serving, GPU economics, pipelines, and observability.

name: Evaluation, Reliability & Security
summary: The part I came in through. Measuring whether a system is right rather than whether it looks right, with pre-registered methods, held-out data, and baselines that are allowed to win.
competencies: Offline evaluation design and held-out splits
LLM-as-judge methods and their failure modes
